quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing the tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing train tracks. Always obey signs and traffic signals. Trains, cars, and bicycles share the same road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are coming to a T intersection.
Your road crosses a divided highway.
You are on a bridge over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road crosses a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two separate one-way roads separated by a median or guide rail.

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Use your turn signal to show other drivers that you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, signal:

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early so others know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early so others know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers have time to know your plans.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout, you should:

options.text: Let the steering wheel move freely.
Let the car slowly come to a stop.
Keep driving until you reach a garage.
Brake hard to stop right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car slowly come to a stop.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and do not brake. Slowly take your foot off the gas and steer in the direction you want to go. Find a safe place to pull over and let your car slow down naturally.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must allow for:

options.text: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
The shorter distance trucks need to stop.
The quieter sound of larger trucks.
The faster speed of larger trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks need more space to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay in places where the truck driver can see you and where your view is not blocked by the truck.

questions.question: When you get in a car to drive, what should you adjust first?

options.text: Your seat belt.
The steering wheel.
Your rearview mirror.
Your seat.

questions.explanation: First adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your new seat position.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive at the speed limit.
Never drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. Low beams help others see you. High beams reflect back into your eyes in fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run into the street without looking.
Only cross with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run into the street without looking.
questions.explanation: Children may not understand danger and can run in front of your car without looking. Slow down and be extra careful where children play.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.
Give pedestrians the right-of-way only when they have the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give pedestrians the right-of-way, even if they are crossing illegally.
questions.explanation: You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter what. Always watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: If you see this sign above your lane, you:

options.text: Cannot exit the freeway.
Can either continue through or exit from your current lane.
Can stay in your lane and continue through.
Must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must exit the freeway if you stay in your current lane.
questions.explanation: An "Exit only" sign means the lane does not continue through the interchange. The lane becomes an exit ramp. You can either change lanes to go through, or you must exit if you stay in that lane.

questions.question: When there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, you should:

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Go between both of them.
Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: Before turning, you should signal:

options.text: Only if other drivers are following you.
When the front of your car reaches the intersection.
Three to four seconds before the intersection.
Two car lengths before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three to four seconds before the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal three to four seconds before turning to give other drivers time to react.

questions.question: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means the vehicle:

options.text: Carries radioactive materials.
Makes wide turns.
Moves slower than normal traffic.
Stops frequently.

questions.explanation: In rural areas, an orange triangle is on farm tractors and horse-drawn vehicles that travel at 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: When a truck driver wants to pass your vehicle:

options.text: Keep your speed steady or slow down.
Stop.
Change lanes.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed steady or slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down slightly and keep a steady speed while the truck passes. Never speed up when a truck is passing you.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must:

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights.
Use parking lights.
Use no lights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in the rain.
